title: Direct-address map steered by a searched three-mode controller
summary: Symbols are written into a direct-address map, one item per address, under a controller with three write disciplines (pairs, positions, depths). Reading fetches the item at an address and can follow it a bounded number of times. The controller setting and an output translation are learned by trying every setting on a few examples.
core_idea: Pair a one-item-per-address map with a small searched controller so that recall, copying, nesting and chained lookups all become address reads.

state.name: T
state.meaning: Direct-address map: T[a] is the item last written under address a; at most C addresses are held at once.

state.name: ctl
state.meaning: Controller registers: mode mu, stop symbol sigma, separators Z, answer set A, hop limit H, held token p, write flag w, position c, emitted count o, depth d; about 16 words plus |A| + |Z|.

state.name: M
state.meaning: Learned translation from a read result to an emitted symbol, at most N entries for an alphabet of N symbols.

update.plain: controller step: the stop symbol sigma ends writing; in pair mode a token waits in p or completes a pair that goes into the store with ins; in string mode each symbol goes in under the running position c; in nesting mode an opener goes in at the raised depth d and a closer takes out the entry at d
update.name: controller

update.latex: \mathrm{ins}(a,b):\; T[a] \leftarrow b \;\; (|T| < C \text{ or } a \in T)
update.plain: ins writes item b under address a, replacing any earlier item there; a write that would exceed C entries is dropped
update.name: write

readout.latex: \mu=0:\; y_0=x_t,\; r_j=\mathrm{get}(y_{j-1}),\; u=r_j \text{ at the first } j\le H \text{ with } r_j\in A,\; u=r_{j-1} \text{ at the first } r_j=\varnothing;\quad \mu=1:\; u=\mathrm{get}(o);\quad \mu=2:\; u=\mathrm{get}(d);\qquad \hat{y}_t = M[u] \text{ for } u\in\mathrm{dom}\,M,\; A_0 \text{ for } u=\varnothing,\; u \text{ otherwise}
readout.plain: read: in pair mode get what is held for the current token and keep following while the result is not in the answer set A, at most H times; in string mode get position o; in nesting mode get depth d; translate through M
readout.name: readout

readout.plain: get returns the item held under address a, or nothing

learning.description: A finite search: the answer set A is collected from the training targets and the separator set Z from the symbols that occur exactly once in every training sequence. For each mode and each stop choice (none or a member of Z) the controller runs over the m sequences, the pairs (read result, target) are tallied, M takes the majority target per read result, and the setting with the highest training accuracy is kept.
learning.few_shot_argument: The space has at most 3(|Z| + 1) + 1 settings plus a majority map, so m = 12 sequences pick the right setting in the small cases (copy and recall at 4, depth 2, composition at 4, binding at 2) on three seeds.

complexity.constants_notes: One map access per fetch, at most H fetches per token, each followed by a membership test against the answer list A; the controller adds a constant.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Search over a handful of controller settings with a majority translation.

prediction.statement: With m = 12 training examples the learned controller reaches accuracy at least 0.99 on copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, nesting at depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops, on three seeds.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: String mode with C = L copies L = 8, 32, 64 over D = 4 with per-string accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = K and H = 1 answers K = 8, 32, 64 with per-query accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words (N = 2K + 17 at K = 64 with V = 16).
Nesting mode with C = depth predicts the legal closer at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2T and H = 2 answers f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32 with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
Pair mode with C = 2(hops + 1) and H = hops + 1 resolves chains of 1, 4, 8 hops with accuracy 1.0 within 2C + N + 16 words.
The search learner reaches 0.99 from m = 12 examples on seeds 0, 1, 2 for copy at L = 4, recall at K = 4, depth 2, composition at T = 4 and binding at 2 hops.

For any fixed capacity C, recall of K = C + 1 distinct pairs over V = 16 symbols fails on some instance: the store holds at most C pairs, so one probe's item is absent and is answered from at most 16 guesses (at C = 64 this is K = 65, above every P2 size).

falsifiers: A P2 instance at the listed sizes that the hand-set controller with this store answers wrongly, or that needs more than 2C + N + 16 words.
A seed on which 12 small-case examples leave the learned controller below 0.99.

toy_example.description: Three pairs written, then three fetches and one chained fetch of two steps.
